_readme: Single source of truth for the documentation guard.
Two consumers read THIS FILE, both through scripts/protected-paths.mjs, and neither
may keep its own copy of the patterns:
`node scripts/verify-protected-paths.mjs` fails if a consumer hardcodes a copy.
model: Rules (docs/rules/), maps (the AGENTS.md files) and records (docs/adr/) have different
owners; docs/rules/DOC-RULES.md says who, and why. agentOwned is the short list of what
ONLY the agent may write. Everything outside these three lists belongs to people.
precedence: humanOwned, then sharedOwned, then agentOwned; the first match decides. A path is protected -- meaning a human may not write it -- if and only if it matches an agentOwned pattern and matches neither of the other two lists. Carve-outs are nested inside guarded directories, so they must be evaluated first and override what follows.
consumers: There are two, and they ask opposite questions of the same lists. The protected-path guard asks 'may a HUMAN write this?' via `--check`, and sharedOwned answers yes. The documentation agent's self-check asks 'may the AGENT keep what it wrote here?' via `--classify`, and both agentOwned and sharedOwned answer yes. Never infer one answer from the other by inverting it.
matching: Patterns are repo-root-relative, forward-slash, case-insensitive globs. `**` matches any number of path segments; `*` and `?` match within a single segment. Paths outside the repository are never protected.

agentOwned.reason: Maps are regenerated from the code on the pull request that changed it, so a hand edit here is overwritten by the next run and fails this check in CI. Change the code and let the map follow.

sharedOwned.owner: people and the documentation agent alike
sharedOwned.reason: A decision record is the one document either may author. The agent proposes one when it spots a decision nobody wrote down, and marks it `status: proposed` with `reasoning: reconstructed` when it inferred the rejected alternative rather than being told. A person authors one when they hold the reasoning, and only a person promotes one to `accepted`. Guarding this against people would make the record unpromotable; guarding it against the agent would discard the proposal it was asked for.

humanOwned.reason: The decision-record form is authored by people; the agent fills it in, it does not redesign it.

guidance: Change the code, and let the documentation agent regenerate the map on the pull request.
If the rule itself is wrong rather than the map, edit it in docs/rules/ - that whole directory is yours.
If this path should not be guarded at all, edit .protected-paths.json - that file is human-owned on purpose.
Set PROTECTED_PATHS_BYPASS=1 in the environment only when setting the harness up for the first time. No workflow sets it; the documentation agent is exempted by commit authorship.
